articles.title: Transformers 8 Casting Details Sound a Lot Like Characters From the First Movie
articles.summary: The next chapter in the live-action Transformers movie franchise is getting underway, and it seems that the new instalment will mark a return to its roots. 2007 saw the release of the first live-action Transformers movie, and Michael Bay's efforts to bring the iconic cartoon franchise to life proved to be far more impressive than […]
articles.content:
Shared by Daniel Richtman on X , the scoop claims that Transformers 8 is “looking for a wisecracking teen outcast who'd rather be streaming on Twitch, raised by a single mom, and a motorcycle-riding young woman in her early 20s who pushes him toward his destiny”. Naturally, these details don't specifically name the characters in question, but the dynamic it suggests is incredibly familiar to fans of the franchise. Reports of Michael Bay's return to the Transformers franchise were the first hint that the next movie is seeking to return to its roots, but these alleged casting details seem to confirm it. However, there's enough ambiguity surrounding the planned movie that, even if the scoop turns out to be accurate, the upcoming film could still be heading in various different directions.

When you look over the Transformers franchise's box office numbers, it's clear that the initial movies remain among its most successful. Michael Bay's Transformers movies managed to add a compelling human element to the story of the Autobots and the Decepticons, and the sheer action spectacle they put on for audiences proved hugely successful. The casting rumors seem in line with previous reports that the movie will be set in the present day, but the dynamic it hints at between the male and female leads is oddly reminiscent of Sam and Mikaela from 2007's Transformers . This suggests a few possible avenues for the upcoming movie, and whichever Transformers 8 opts to take, it could spell more success for the franchise.

The first and perhaps most obvious implication of the “wisecracking outcast” and the “motorcycle-riding young woman who pushes him toward his destiny” is that Transformers 8 will serve as a full reboot of the live-action franchise. As the many sequels have added numerous characters and plot points to the franchise, it may well be time for a fresh start that brings the most iconic characters back to the fore. The original trilogy, which followed Sam and Mikaela — the latter for the first two movies, at least — remains the most successful era of the live-action franchise, so rebooting the story makes sense on multiple levels. However, this isn't the only route Transformers 8 could take.

There's also a strong possibility that the upcoming movie will continue the live-action franchise in a more traditional sense, introducing all-new characters to the wider continuity. The reported casting details might simply indicate an attempt to recapture the dynamic of the first movie, as the characters and their story clearly resonated with audiences. Doing so would subtly revisit one of the best Transformers movies without totally erasing previous chapters, allowing Transformers 8 to evoke the franchise's past while setting up a bold new future. With Michael Bay's rumored return and the passing of Transformers icon Peter Cullen, it seems that Transformers 8 will be a defining new chapter for the franchise, and a potential return to its roots might be just what it needs to get back to major box office success.

How do you feel about Transformers 8 ? Can it breathe new life into the franchise in light of Michael Bay and Steven Spielberg's return? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.summary: Pattinson's Bond casting has broken the internet.
articles.content:
Yesterday the internet exploded when it was revealed that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond in Denis Villeneuve 's developing 26th movie in the franchise. Fans had big reactions to this 007 news , and plenty of other figured in Hollywood have also weighed in. I didn't have Brad Pitt sharing his views on my bingo card, but why not?

There you have it. Amidst all the discourse about the casting news, the Fight Club actor approves of Pattinson becoming the next 007 after Daniel Craig's Bond films . He's clearly been impressed with the talents for the Twilight actor, who has had a truly busy year thanks to roles in The Drama , The Odyssey , and Dune: Part Three . We'll just have to wait and see what he brings to the table as everyone's favorite MI6 agent.

Honestly, sign me up. While the response to Pattinson's casting has been mixed, I have to assume that fans of the Bond films would love to see Brad Pitt play a villain in the beloved franchise. This is no confirmation that he's actually being considered for a role, but perhaps these comments will get back to Villeneuve and inspire him to set up a meeting. I'm definitely going to keep my fingers crossed.

articles.title: 'Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother' DP On Balancing Action Sequences With A Man's "Spiritual Journey And Struggles Of Trying To Step Up As A Father" — ToruńCamerimage
articles.summary: When cinematographer Katelin Arizmendi boarded Bassam Tariq’s genre-defying sophomore feature film Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, the pair were both new to the action genre and a key challenge they faced during the 30-day shoot was making sure action sequences didn’t drown out the emotional core of the film. “We knew that we were […]
articles.content:
When cinematographer Katelin Arizmendi boarded Bassam Tariq 's genre-defying sophomore feature film Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother , the pair were both new to the action genre and a key challenge they faced during the 30-day shoot was making sure action sequences didn't drown out the emotional core of the film.

"We knew that we were making a movie with action, but we knew that we weren't making an action movie," Arizmendi tells Deadline during the ToruńCamerimage Film Festival.

The action drama stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devout Muslim contract killer and grieving widower in Houston whose life is upended when he must balance raising his three young children – including a newborn daughter in urgent need of breast milk – while pulled into a violent conflict with a religious extremist group. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Festivals 'Fatherland' Takes Top Prize At ToruńCamerimage; 'Wild Horse Nine' Wins Audience Award News 'Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother' Star Mahershala Ali Says It Can Be "Dangerous That People End Up Believing Their Own Righteousness" -- Contenders L.A.

"We knew that the visual language needed to be built off of the journey of the characters and the emotion and the perspective of Latif first," says Arizmendi. "Both of us were new to action. Bassam had almost shot Blade and then I did second unit on Dune , so I had shot action, but I hadn't ever been the main DP to design action films and action sequences. So, it was trying to marry the two so that the action felt exciting and it felt studio level and theatrical but that it didn't feel like a different movie, because really the core of the story is this family and this man's journey and his spiritual journey and his struggles of trying to step up as a father while dealing with the loss of his love and the mother of his three children. There were so many things that were driving the visual language." Early conversations, she says, involved making sure to spotlight Latif's teenage daughter Fatiha (played by Adia) because of the impact she had on Latif throughout the story.

"I wanted her to visually hold as much weight in each frame because she's always standing up to him and shining a light back on him to reflect himself and she challenges him," she says. "So, I wanted her to have a strong presence." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Key fight sequences, she says, were initially challenging. "I knew how I didn't want them to look almost more than I knew how I wanted them to look at first," she says.

"I knew I didn't want them to go handheld, and I knew I wanted the rest of the film to have much more calm, precise camera movements so I didn't want the action to go handheld. We talked about that with the stunt coordinator very early on. I knew that we also needed to keep in tune with the emotion of each fight sequence, so it wasn't like there was no purpose to any of it. We needed to stay grounded in where Latif's emotional journey was throughout each fight."

Arizmendi also points to the significance of the high angle shots, which feature throughout the film: "I wanted to play with these high angles as him being judged by a higher power and so those either come before or after the violence."

The Amazon/MGM Studios film has a very rich and textured color palate, something that Arizmendi notes was born after she attended a prayer service at a mosque, which gave her a sense of how deep the colors needed to feel on screen.

"It started there with knowing how rich and saturated we wanted the film to look as well and then in contrast, the Christians are wearing white and camouflage and are brightly lit," she says. "We also had discussions about prayer times in Islam, which I didn't know so much and that was really important because it dictates where the sun is. We talked about that really early on and I put that into my lookbook as well because it needed to be really honest."

articles.title: Taylor Swift’s Comments About Friendship Hit Even Harder Amidst Karlie Kloss And Blake Lively Updates
articles.summary: Swift's friend group has evolved over the years.
articles.content:
It’s no secret that Taylor Swift has amassed a large group of celebrity friends. Selena Gomez , Ed Sheeran and Sabrina Carpenter are just a few of the big names that make up Swift’s personal orbit. The beloved pop star has spoken quite a bit about friendship over the years and, most recently, she spoke about it in reference to her involvement with the 2026 movie schedule entry Toy Story 5 . Swift’s latest sentiments on the subject are particularly poignant given where she reportedly stands with Karlie Kloss and Blake Lively.

For the latest Toy Story film, Swift wrote and recorded an original song , “I Knew It, I Knew You,” and it’s currently nominated for two Grammy Awards. Swift has been making the rounds amid awards season, helping the Pixar team promote the legacy sequel, which seems to be a serious contender for some major awards. During a press conference, Swift discussed (via Hello! ) the acclaimed movie’s theme of friendship and stressed the importance of someone looking back on such intimate bonds. She also said this:

The “Delicate” performer’s comments fall directly in line with the narrative of the new Toy Story film, which sees young Bonnie attempting to make genuine friendships. At the same time, cowgirl doll Jessie also reflects fondly on the bond she had with her former owner, Emily. Those plot threads culminated into a truly sentimental third act for the billion-dollar-grossing film. Aside from that, though, Swift’s thoughts are indeed sweet, and they do speak to the nature of how friends come in and out of our lives as time goes on.

The Swift/Kloss friendship began in 2012 after the two publicly showed admiration for each other, and they remained tight until rumors of a falling-out between the two surfaced in 2018., By 2019, it was alleged that Kloss’ continued friendship with former talent manager Scooter Braun (who was in conflict with Swift over her music catalogue) served as a point of contention. While Swift and Kloss wouldn’t be spotted publicly for years after that, the latter surprisingly attended an Eras Tour show . Also, Kloss’ presence at Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in July 2026 and her subsequent attendance at Chiefs games also seemed to suggest the two were friends again.

articles.title: PS2 Game From 2001 Now Free for Some PS5 and PS4 Users
articles.summary: A PS2 action-adventure game from 2001 is now free for some PS5 and PS4 users with a PlayStation Plus subscription. Specifically, a PS Plus Premium subscription. In this case, an Essential or Extra subscription is insufficient. Meanwhile, the game is available, whenever it goes live today, on the PlayStation Store as an individual purchase, but […]
articles.content:
Back on October 20, 2001, almost exactly 25 years ago, developer Crystal Dynamics and publisher Eidos Interactive — before both were acquired by Square Enix and then sold to Embracer Group — released Soul Reaver 2 on the PS2, and the PS2 only. This was before the former would become the developer behind the Tomb Raide r series, which it would ultimately become best known for. Prior to this, it was best known for series such as Gex and Legacy of Kain . It's the latter that Soul Reaver 2 is a part of.

Soul Reaver 2 is the third game in the Legacy of Kain series and a sequel to Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver , the second game in the series. Back in the day, it earned a solid 80 on Metacritic upon release, and in the years to come, it became a bit of a cult classic, similar to the series as a whole. This isn't to say it didn't sell well, because it did. It became part of Sony's ‘Greatest Hits' list, but it wasn't a smash mainstream hit. In 2021, it was remastered and re-released on the PlayStation Store as Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver 1 & 2 Remastered . It's not this version that is free, but the PS2 original.

A 2001 PS2 Game in 2026 As you may expect, Soul Reaver 2 doesn't hold up very well in 2026, hence the need for a remaster. This isn't a slight against it, but just how it is with early 3D games, which were very primitive in design and rough around the edges. To this end, those interested in checking it out for the first time in 2026 are unlikely to walk away with an incredible impression. That said, for those with 2001 PS2 nostalgia eating away at their soul, it still does hit.

Better yet, the game isn't very long, only taking about 9 to 13 hours, depending on variables like playstyle and completion rate. This makes it very accessible in an age where many games are tediously long. That said, if this doesn't tickle your fancy, there are a variety of other new PlayStation Plus free games . Meanwhile, if this PS2 nostalgia isn't your PS2 nostalgia, a great PS2 trilogy was recently made available on PS5 and PS4 for just $2.49 .

articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Is a Beautiful Adaptation, But Doesn't Quite Achieve Its Potential [REVIEW]
articles.summary: There is something a bit ironic about The Hunger Games franchise. A dystopian world where the suffering and death of innocents at the behest of a brutal government and society in the name of entertainment being turned into big screen entertainment for the masses, at times, feels a little on the nose. But, over the […]
articles.content:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping takes us back 24 years before Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark’s games to the Second Quarter Quell, not only finally giving us Haymitch’s origin story, but also revealing that the fires of revolution that would ultimately catch and burn down the Capitol’s brutal hold on the Districts started not with Katniss’ defiance, but with Haymitch’s determination to not be a pawn and the quiet efforts of a much larger cast of allies than one might have expected. For fans of Suzanne Collins’ beloved book series — as well as for fans of the original films — it’s a story that they’ve longed to see told on the big screen and while the film delivers a phenomenal cast, brilliant acting, and a story that really lands certain elements of just how dark the Capitol really is, certain elements from the book are compressed or absent and one of the most anticipated moments ultimately doesn’t quite hit, leaving us with a movie that is genuinely good, but not quite hitting full potential.

One of the biggest challenges that Sunrise on the Reaping has going into it even if you haven’t read the book is that, in the larger sense, we already know how the story ends. After all, original The Hunger Games films ended with the fall of the Capitol and the of the Games. We also already know going into things that Haymitch survives his games and has a brutal time after. It feels like an odd place to start already knowing so much, but the film actually uses this place of knowledge to its favor. We’re not so much being told the story but being shown the people in it and in that respect, the film excels. Every single role in Sunrise on the Reaping is perfectly cast. Joseph Zada in particular does a phenomenal job as Haymitch, introducing us to a young man whose life is full of joy and love who slowly and steadily becomes someone else as his experiences in the arena and after the games permanently change him into the grumpy alcoholic we met in The Hunger Games . It’s a transformation that happens fast, but Zada does a haunting job of making us walk with Haymitch as he fights for his humanity every step of the way.

Mckenna Grace also shines as Maysilee Donner, but the performance that may be the most surprising standout is that of Jesse Plemons as Plutarch Heavensbee. As a cameraman for the Hunger Games, he’s responsible for much of the storytelling and is complicit in the capitol’s propaganda machine, but there is much more to him than what is on the surface. We already know how he fits into the story in the future, but seeing his efforts a quarter century before Katniss changes everything has massive impact thanks in no small part to the nuance Plemons brings to the performance. No one in the movie is simply black and white, and all of the shades of gray shine through.

But while we get all of the shades of gray with the characters in the story, the actual visuals in Sunrise on the Reaping are in wildly brilliant color. From the lethal beauty of the arena itself, to the vibrance of the Tribute Parade, the splendor and extravagance of the Capitol is on display like we’ve never seen before. Even the interiors at the training center and in the tribute’s quarters are rich with colorful details. There’s a retrofuturisitc vibe to just about everything in the Capitol parts of the film that is just exquisitely done, even if it does feel a little dated — something Elle Fanning’s Effie Trinket even comments on at one point.

What works about this is that it’s not only a visual feast — the mutts in particular are gloriously horrific — but it all highlights the superficiality of the Capitol in a way that feels different than what we’ve seen in previous films. The sets here are brighter, louder, and more “cheap” in the way that only expensive things trying too hard to be classy can be cheap. It makes for a great visual contrast to the humanity of the characters as well as a cue that signals that we’re at the very beginning of what will eventually be huge changes in this world. This version of the Capitol is starting to go out of fashion; it just doesn’t quite know it yet.

Even with truly great performances and visuals that does a brilliant storytelling job alongside the acting and actual story, while Sunrise on the Reaping is a strong adaptation it does still come up just a little short. Specifically, there are elements of the story from the book that are compressed that ultimately rob the film of some of the darkness that makes Haymitch’s story really work. The biggest instance of this is Lou Lou. It is no secret that Lou Lou is the body double that the Capitol replaces Louella McCoy with after she’s killed during the Tribute Parade, but the horror of Lou Lou’s existence is much more fleshed out in the book. In the book, those details matter — Lou Lou is disturbing to those around her but also a heartbreaking figure as the suffering she’s undergoing as a puppet of the Capitol is revealed. That's not present in the movie.

The quiet horror of this girl having no real identity of her own has a significant impact on Haymitch, something that the film loses entirely by almost sanitizing Lou Lou as a character. It also has the effect of dulling the viciousness of the Capitol, which Lou Lou and her fate — as well as the questions about her identity — are perhaps the harshest examples of. Without the tragedy of Lou Lou’s “backstory,” her demise just doesn’t pay off the way it should.

There’s also the matter of the appearances by Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, and Woody Harrelson. While those returns might be what Hunger Games fans were most looking forward to, the way it actually is delivered feels less like a beautiful full circle moment of triumph and, instead, like thin fan service. Fans will love it, but it doesn’t really offer anything important to the story.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is a good movie. It’s honestly a very good adaptation of what might be one of the best books in Suzanne Collins’ overall Hunger Games series. Much about the film makes it easily the best-made in the entire franchise and it truly has some of the best performances as well. But while it is good it falls just short of greatness. The potential is there; it is just ultimately unrealized but it still makes for a fitting (presumably) final chapter in the saga.

Political ad spending on the 2025-26 election cycle topped more than $12 billion, a particular boon to broadcasters, streamers and digital outlets.

The figures for the 2025-26 cycle are from a new report from analysis firm AdImpact .

Per the firm, this was the first midterm election to outspend a presidential cycle, with spending 8% above 2024, when spending was $11.2 billion. It also was 35% about the 2022 midterm and three times the 2018 cycle.

Broadcast saw $5.85 billion in political ad revenue, up 9% from 2024, while its share actually grew from 48% to 49%. Streaming, or connected TV, grew by 14% to $2.66 billion and digital rose by 11% to $1.91 billion. articles.title: IDW Crime Goes Literally Bananas With New Series, Rotten [EXCLUSIVE]
articles.summary: This spring, crime came to IDW. The new imprint, IDW Crime, brought thrilling, complex stories that includes murder mysteries like Seven Wives, the twisted alliance between a serial killer and true-crime influencer in Killer Influences, and even a fan-convention thriller where everyone is a suspect in Fixation. Now, IDW Crime’s world is getting a little […]
articles.content:
Hitting comic shops on February 24, 2027, is Rotten . Written by Mark Russell with art by John Bivens, Rotten is a five issue limited series that will see a high school prank take a much darker turn, exposing something truly rotten in the town of Gilbert, Florida. Pre-orders for the series are due January 18, 2027. We’ve also got a first look at Rotten’s covers and trust us — you’ve never seen anything quite like this and you don’t want to miss it.

In Rotten , Something is rotten in Gilbert, Florida. And when five local high school seniors plan to heist Big Mike, the world’s largest anthropomorphic banana statue, they’ll peel back decades’ worth of corruption. Once home to a booming banana plantation, Gilbert is now where the American dream comes to die, and at the center of the decaying town stands Big Mike. Formerly a herald of greatness, the 15-food smiling banana is now just a quirky roadside attraction and the mascot of the town’s annual Banana Fest.

To seniors Abby, Tony, Vincent, Victor, Millie, and Steve, though, Big Mike is their way out. Graduation is looming, abut with families to support and parental expectations to dodge, the kids know they’ll never escape Gilbert…until Abby, the mayor’s daughter, suggests a heist: Steal Big Mike and hold him for ransom. They demand $200,000, hoping it’ll be enough for tickets out of town and college tuition. But their quest for freedom might not be so simple. From Mark Russell and artist John Bivens comes Rotten , a crime story fruitful with action and heart. One thing’s for sure…this sh*t is about to get bananas.

While the idea of a banana-themed heist story might seem out there, the story of Rotten also has a core that anyone can identify with: those last moments of transition between childhood and adulthood. It sounds like Rotten is more than just an insane, fruit-themed heist caper, but a wild coming of age story as well, something that makes it all the more interesting (and all the more insane as well).

“It’s rare for me to want to write a story that I myself didn’t come up with the idea for,” Russell said. “But when editor Riley Farmer approached me with the premise for Rotten , the story of a group of teens living in a dead-end town, a banana-themed town, no less. And that it becomes a heist story? It just sounded too off-the-wall not to write. As I started working on the story in my mind, I realized that, as crazy as the premise was, it was a story about a group of friends who are going through what we all go through. Namely, the moment when you realize that if you all follow your dreams, you might never see each other again. And yet, you still want to help each other go through that door, whatever’s on the other side. I’m not going to lie, this story takes some pretty WTF turns, but at its heart, it’s about biting off more than you can chew because you know there are people you can trust to help you eat it.”

And of course, things will get bananas in more way than one, at least according to Bivens.

“I got a breakdown of the concept sent to me by editor Riley Farmer, and it was bananas,” Bivens said. “Literally, there were bananas in the story… and a giant banana that was pretty important to the whole thing. This was a different kind of project for me which is a bonus (if anyone has read my work, they probably think I’m the weird horror guy). Throw in crime that feels very ‘Florda man’, and an ’80s nostalgia for the teens-in-trouble trope, and I was happy to sign on.”

Rotten goes on sale from IDW Crime on February 24, 2027. Pre orders are due by January 18, 2027.

Will you be checking out this bananas new comic (get it?) Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Review: A Worthier Prequel to the Dystopian Battle Royale, Powered by Joseph Zada’s Star-Making Turn
articles.summary: The ensemble of Francis Lawrence’s saga of fascism and rebellion also features Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning.
articles.content:
The sixth movie in the $3.3 billion Hunger Games franchise contends, like many series entries before it, with a somewhat jarring tonal discordancy between the glitzy spectacle and grotesque political satire of the Capitol and the emotionally loaded brutality of the Arena, where children and teens from each of the 12 districts of Panem are forced to fight for their lives until only one is standing. But Sunrise on the Reaping overcomes that imbalance because the horror of the survival battle and the sorrow of the losses sustained are rendered with as much scalding pathos as suspense and excitement. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Dual Oscar Winner Christopher Hampton Calls Glenn Close Honorary Oscar "the Least They Can Do," Says AI Is Just "a Super Google" Movies Governors Awards: Glenn Close, Ridley Scott and Floyd Norman Accept Honorary Oscars, Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler Receive Thalberg Award

Francis Lawrence , who has directed all but the first of the features adapted from Suzanne Collins ' hugely popular YA novels, knows what he's doing. But the surprise asset here is Australian actor Joseph Zada in a breakout performance as 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy, the rebellious victor of the 50th Hunger Games. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping The Bottom Line Delivers on emotion and brutal spectacle. Release date : Friday, Nov. 20 Cast : Joseph Zada, Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace, Maya Hawke, Whitney Peak, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Ben Wang, Billy Porter, Molly McCann, Iona Bell, Lili Taylor, Percy Daggs IV, Iris Apatow, Edvyn Ryding, Jhaleil Swaby, Laura Marcus, Scot Greenan Director : Francis Lawrence Screenwriters : Billy Ray, Michael Lesslie, based on the novel by Suzanne Collins Rated PG-13, 2 hours 43 minutes

Played as an adult by Woody Harrelson in the first four films, Haymitch was subsequently forced to serve as a mentor to contestants every year but remained furtively on the side of the resistance. Zada (seen recently as Cal on Netflix's East of Eden ) doesn't have much physical resemblance to Harrelson, but the voice is convincingly that of the Haymitch we know, coming into manhood with firm convictions born out of injustice and providing a resonant link to the earlier films.

Invested with tenacity, kindness and heartrending vulnerability by Zada, Haymitch provides a much more poignant and involving origin story than that of Coriolanus Snow in the lumbering first prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes . The autocratic Capitol leader would go on to consolidate his power by using the televised Games to keep the Panem population scared and under control. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Set 40 years after Songbirds and Snakes and 24 years before the first Hunger Games movie, Sunrise on the Reaping opens on Haymitch's 16th birthday, which coincides with the second Quarter Quell, when the names of "tributes" from each district are drawn to enter the Arena. Being a special edition that happens just once every 25 years, the traditional choice of one male and one female has been doubled to two of each.

Haymitch initially is not among the four selected tributes for District 12, the grimly industrial coal mining sector where everyone appears to be living on or below the poverty line. But when one of the chosen boys tries to make a run for it and is shot by the Stormtrooper-like "Peacekeepers," Haymitch is drawn into a skirmish and dropped into the vacant slot as punishment.

The showbiz cynicism of the operation is illustrated by Plutarch Heavensbee — Jesse Plemons in the role previously played by Philip Seymour Hoffman as an older man, following his promotion to Head Gamekeeper. Designated by the Capitol to oversee the nationwide broadcast, Plutarch dashes about giving camera directions and insisting on do-overs to maximize the drama of tributes being painfully separated from their loved ones and ushered off to almost certain death. As in the propaganda films of most dictatorial regimes, the heavily edited televised content removes all signs of messy rebellion and anti-Capitol sentiment.

The separation is especially wrenching for Haymitch from his widowed mother and adoring younger brother, but equally or perhaps even more so from his girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird ( Whitney Peak ), who tends geese on her father's farm. (She's a descendant of Lucy Gray Baird, the winner of the 10th Hunger Games, played by Rachel Zegler in Songbirds and Snakes .) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The sobriety of the farewells, however, is undercut by the unrestrained caricatures of some high-ranking Capitol officials. Every time the movie lurches into high-camp excess it lessens the emotional weight. The most intrusive example is Glenn Close , exploring new frontiers for over-the-top as Drusilla Sickle, her contemptuous cruelty fueled by her indignation over being assigned to chaperone the District 12 tributes, whom she regards as grimy subhumans.

Wheeled out onstage like Hannibal Lecter to draw the lottery, Drusilla is trussed up in what looks like a leather bumblebee costume, with a red Aunt Gladys wig topped by a raven fascinator, crazy-lady makeup and a mouthful of prosthetic dentures that even Tilda Swinton might balk at. All the better to chomp on the scenery. Shrieking like a pantomime dame, Close goes full Norma Desmond and then flips to Joan Crawford mode, losing her shit with a riding crop (see 1955's Queen Bee ) when she's sassed by Haymitch's smart-mouthed fellow tribute Maysilee ( Mckenna Grace ), a shopkeeper's daughter.

Even higher on the shrill scale is Drusilla's husband, Capitol stylist Magno Stift (Billy Porter), sashaying around in extravagant finery with tiny live golden snakes as earrings. He declines to dress the District 12 unfortunates, sharing his lunatic wife's opinion that they are not fit for couture. Mercifully, Magno is not around for long, making way for the familiar figure of Effie Trinket ( Elle Fanning , amusingly playing a younger version of the character originated onscreen by Elizabeth Banks). The future chaperone briskly takes charge of 12's tributes, giving their outfits an elegant upgrade before the opening ceremony chariot parade. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

While Fanning gives Effie a shot of humanity beneath her giddy glam manner, the same cannot be said of Kieran Culkin as preening TV broadcast host Caesar Flickerman. "Look alive, children, while you still can!" he tells the tributes in a bit of gallows humor that might have been funny had he not been so obnoxiously glib. Where Stanley Tucci offset Caesar's callous showmanship with mischievous charisma in the first films, Culkin just plays sarcastic mockery. His Caesar is a charmless creep.

While the sinister combination of razzle-dazzle and fascist barbarity has always been essential to the Hunger Games world, it's a relief here when the Capitol monsters take a backseat to the young people whose lives hang in the balance. From the very beginning, we see what a beloved figure Haymitch is in the village, how pure is the love he shares with Lenore and how tender and reassuring he is with the youngest of the district's tributes, Louella (Molly McCann).

They make a pact to be allies, extending also to Maysilee and fourth District 12 tribute Wyatt (Ben Wang), even if his sideline as an oddsmaker on the Games earns him some initial distrust. But when tragedy strikes early on during the chariot parade, Haymitch stares down Coriolanus Snow, his eyes expressing fury, disgust and defiance. While that uneasy moment will be cut for the broadcast, it was witnessed by the public at the opening ceremony, an embarassment to Snow that puts a target on Haymitch's back. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Played as a youth by Tom Blyth in Songbirds and Snakes and by Donald Sutherland as an older man in the original Hunger Games quadrilogy, Snow here has the soft-spoken menace and steely authority of Ralph Fiennes . His intelligence is unquestionable but he's also paranoid and gullible about his consigliere Plutarch and given to fits of petulant rage.

The certainty that Snow will ensure he dies an agonizing death in the Arena makes Haymitch rethink his alliances, telling the other District 12 tributes that it's not safe to be around him. But he does enter cautiously into a pact with Ampert (Percy Daggs IV) from District 3, who informs him that other districts are open to collaboration in order to prevail over the elite contestants from Districts 1 and 2. Known as Career tributes, these are the most frequent victors in the Games, due to their wealth, privilege and extensive combat and weaponry training.

Ampert was entered into the games by Snow in retaliation for the attempt to sabotage Capitol communications by the boy's father, Beetee (Kelvin Harrison Jr.), now forced to serve as a mentor but still secretly plotting. The mentors specifically assigned to District 12 are past victors Wiress (Maya Hawke) and Mags (Lili Taylor); neither actor is given a lot to do but they are a welcome presence — warm, supportive and candid with the tributes.

Lawrence and screenwriters Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie have relatively little time and breathing room to give the more ruthless Arena opponents much character definition. But two District 1 Careers are memorably lethal — Silka (Laura Marcus) with her double-headed axes and muscle-bound Panache (Jhaleil Swaby) with his ferocious anger and strength. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The nail-biting Arena action is vicious and bloody, sustaining high stakes as Haymitch attempts to break the Capitol's brain hub, which sends in "mutts" — genetically modified animals, from electrified butterflies to killer squirrels and birds — to overwhelm the tributes earmarked for death.

Zada is the beating heart of the film, mutinous but neither cocky nor fearless, and he has stirring scenes with Ampert and Maysilee. The hair from one of Britney Spears' blonde bangs periods is a distraction, but Grace is fiery in the latter role — gutsy, determined and a loyal friend to Haymitch once their allegiance is cemented. She's also handy with a poisoned blow dart. Iona Bell as a young substitute tribute drugged into compliance by the Capitol also has touching moments.

Other cast standouts are Peak, lovely as Haymitch's sweetheart; and the always dependable Plemons, who deftly navigates Plutarch's double duty as a Capitol official playing for the other side.

Bolstered by DP Jo Willems' muscular camerawork, James Newton Howard's soaring score and Uli Hanisch's imaginative production design, Sunrise on the Reaping is a return, after the disappointing Songbirds and Snakes , to the spirit of the first movies. There's even a brief appearance by baby Katniss Everdeen to complete the circle. It's impossible not to feel sympathy when young people are being sacrificed in horrific ways for the ritualistic entertainment of the masses and the power-flexing of a pitiless overlord. A moving coda set many years later re-introduces familiar faces that will add to the satisfaction for longtime franchise fans.

articles.title: Ta-Nehisi Coates, Kamilah Forbes and Kenyatta Matthews Formally Launch Maceo-Lyn Productions
articles.summary: The production company is backing 'When A Witness Recants' and the film adaptation of 'The Water Dancer,' among other projects.
articles.content:
Ta-Nehisi Coates , Kamilah Forbes and Kenyatta Matthews are formally announcing their company, Maceo-Lyn Productions, with the premiere of the HBO Original documentary When A Witness Recants.

The documentary, which airs Nov. 17, is one of several projects at the production company, including the upcoming feature film adaptation of The Water Dancer, the debut novel from Coates. Forbes is also directing the Broadway play Mix and Master, starring Tony Award winners Kara Young and Ruben Santiago-Hudson, in January 2027, as well as Boom for Real, a new musical in development about Jean-Michel Basquiat with a score by John Legend.

The company was formed in 2020, with the documentary film adaptation of Coates' Between the World and Me , as their first project. Forbes directed the film, and helmed the prior stage adaptation.

While Coates said he didn't set out to create a production company ("I actually wanted nothing to do with Hollywood at all," Coates said), he valued working with close collaborators on the project. Matthews and Forbes became friends in middle school, and then met Coates at Howard University, with Matthews later marrying Coates.

"I think there was a level of trust between the three of us, and it was quite clear that we probably would continue to work in that space after this, even though it wasn't a thing I necessarily saw for myself. I just did not want to be in business with people who I did not have a deep understanding of, and who did not have a deep understanding of me, both aesthetically and ideologically," Coates told The Hollywood Reporter .

Forbes, former executive producer at the Apollo, notes that they're prioritizing quality over quantity, with the projects meant to appeal to their varied backgrounds in journalism and writing, theater, as well as social activism, with a focus on Black storytelling and moving the culture forward.

"I think it comes to what's moving us?" Forbes said. "I think our partnership is really unique simply because we come to storytelling from several different corners."

"What moves the needle for us. What are the stories that we're just haunted by?," added Matthews. In the case of When A Witness Recants, which follows the wrongful murder conviction of three Baltimore teenagers, Matthews notes that she became fixated on the story after staying up late reading the 2021 New Yorker article. Coates, who grew up in the same neighborhood, had been similarly fixated by the case.

Future work is expected to span across film, television and theater, scripted and non-scripted, with the trio teasing an upcoming documentary about historical figures.

"One of the things that we really do prize at Maceo-Lyn, we value words. I mean, we can't not with Ta-Nehisi being one of the three prongs of the company, and so we always start with what is the written piece that moves us. Be it a script, be it a magazine article, be it a play," Matthews said.

Coates noted that he is excited to see the feature film adaptation of his debut novel, about a man born into slavery with the power to transport himself long distances, which has been in the works since 2019 with Brad Pitt's Plan B.

"There's been some changes in the industry that presented some challenges, but I think nonetheless both Kenyatta and Kamilah and our partners over at Plan B, we're really excited about bringing that to film. It's one of these things where you can't get it wrong. I mean, something about making a bad slavery film is significantly worse than just making a bad film," Coates said.

articles.title: James Bond Is Unlikely to Ever Evolve as a Franchise, But Here's Why People Keep Watching
articles.summary: His name is Bond. James Bond. He’s a fictional British secret service agent, originally from Ian Fleming’s 1950s novels and short story collections, but he made the big screen in the ‘60s. Since his initial portrayal by Sean Connery, Bond, or as he’s better known, 007, has been a household name. Even if people haven’t […]
articles.content:
With Amazon taking over the franchise with Robert Pattinson in the lead role , there have been reports of a new origin for the character. Given the choice to go with a more youthful actor, a change from the last Bond, James Bond 26 is likely to go into the character’s backstory and show us a James Bond new to the service, instead of one who has been 007 for a while. Steven Knight has boasted of being given more leeway with the character , but it feels unlikely that he’ll be that different when he makes his way to our screens. Still, that may just be what makes the character work and keeps an audience for a franchise that, more than ever, is at risk of becoming irrelevant.

The cultural impact of James Bond cannot be overstated. A mere four years after Dr. No ’s release in 1962, there were 22 secret agent films released, many trying to tap into the Bond franchise’s success and pop culture dominance. The protagonists were either Bond lookalikes or intentionally anti-Bonds of a harsher background than a reserve Navy member. “Bond. James Bond” is often referred to as the most loved and well-known one-liner in film, especially for British cinema-goers, and the film franchise is, decades-wise, the longest-running film series.

With many of the films as straight adaptations of the Ian Fleming novels, the immersion crafted by Fleming seems vital to the franchise. Fleming described his intention for his first Bond novel as wanting to “write the spy story to end all spy stories”, and based James Bond on people he had met during his time in WWII. With an intentionally plain-sounding name, James Bond was meant to be “a neutral figure —an anonymous, blunt instrument wielded by a government department.”

James Bond as a franchise wasn’t afraid to lean into the spirit of the times — see the 1979 film Moonraker, which ultimately took James Bond to space and embraced more sci-fi elements — but inevitably returns to its basics. 2006’s Casino Royale was a soft reboot of the franchise, not in line with the loose continuity of the previous films, and stripped away the gadgets that had distracted from the character. Critics and fans alike rejoiced to see Bond return to his roots.

With the confirmed reports of Robert Pattinson’s casting — after weeks of speculation among the Bond hopefuls — the Daniel Craig era has officially come to an end. From 2006 to 2021, Craig played Bond in five films amid a shifting cultural landscape. Other notable British franchises, such as Doctor Who and Sherlock Holmes , experimented with changing the quote-unquote look of their main character. To considerable backlash, Doctor Who cast Jodie Whittaker as the 13th Doctor, with her playing the main role from 2018 to 2021, and years later cast Ncuti Gatwa as the 15th. A CBS loose adaptation of Sherlock Holmes cast Lucy Liu as a female Watson in Elementary, which ran from 2012 to 2019, and Japan’s Miss Sherlock cast both Holmes and Watson as women, becoming the first show to cast a woman as Sherlock Holmes.

Around this time, the idea of a different 007 gained popularity — Daniel Craig frequently fielded questions from the press regarding whether he would be on board with a female James Bond. Craig was against the idea, but mainly out of his exhaustion with the character of 007, not an aversion to seeing women and actors of color as Bond-adjacent spies. Notably, Craig fired back: “Why should a woman play James Bond when there should be a part just as good as James Bond, but for a woman?”

Previous franchise producer Barbara Broccoli asserted that race is not an essential tenant of James Bond’s character, “but he is male.” During press for No Time to Die, both Barbara Broccoli and Phoebe Waller-Bridge admitted the original Bond’s attitude towards women needed to change with the times, but that the character himself is still relevant.

Robert Pattinson is arguably one of the most popular actors working in Hollywood today. In 2026 alone, he starred in The Drama and Primetime with notable feature roles in The Odyssey and Dune: Part Three. Although delayed, audiences are excited for his return as Bruce Wayne / Batman in The Batman Pt. II , and pretty much any residual criticism of him that’s lasted from his Twilight teen heartthrob days is gone.

Bringing a skilled actor like Pattinson to James Bond not only gives the franchise a fresher face, but also electrifying charisma. Given his numerous acting credits, Pattinson may not need James Bond , but James Bond could very well need him. James Bond is beloved, but Pattinson and a fresh script have the potential to make it a must-watch for the power of the writing and performances, and not for nostalgia. Although looking not much different than how Bond has looked in the past — aside from Robert Pattinson being a brunette — there are quite a few ways for Pattinson to bring fresh life to the character. He could follow in Craig’s footsteps with a cerebrally intense portrayal, or perhaps brush off the comedic chops and lean into the character’s history.

What direction do you want from James Bond? Was Pattinson the right choice? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Kevin Feige Just Made A Gambit-Related Promise With Avengers: Doomsday (And I'm Relieved)
articles.summary: I love a good Cajun accent joke, but...
articles.content:
I absolutely loved Channing Tatum 's Gambit in Deadpool & Wolverine . His ridiculous Cajun accent, the way Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool couldn't understand half of what he was saying, and the fact that Tatum finally got to play the character after years of trying made his appearance one of my favorite parts of the movie. But with Gambit returning for Avengers: Doomsday on the 2026 movie schedule , I've been wondering whether Marvel would give him more to do than make everybody laugh. Thankfully, Kevin Feige has some reassuring news.

That's exactly what I was hoping to hear. Don't get me wrong, I laughed every time Gambit opened his mouth in Deadpool & Wolverine . Watching the Merc with the Mouth struggle to decipher his thick accent was hilarious, especially when he asked whether the Minions were his dialect coach. But I also want to see Tatum get a chance to actually play Gambit as a full-fledged character. After all, the mutant hero has quite a bit more going for him than an accent and a deck of exploding playing cards.

For years, the actor tried to get a standalone Gambit movie made at 20th Century Fox. The project went through numerous delays and creative changes before Disney acquired the studio, and the film was ultimately canceled. Then Ryan Reynolds helped bring Tatum's version of the mutant to life in 2024, finally giving him the opportunity he'd been chasing for the better part of a decade.

Of course, there's still plenty we don't know about his role in the epic comic book movie. Doomsday is bringing back several familiar X-Men, including James Marsden 's Cyclops, Ian McKellen 's Magneto and Patrick Stewart 's Professor X. Empire also revealed a new look at Gambit alongside Cyclops outside the X-Mansion, which is pretty cool considering Tatum never got to appear alongside the original team during Fox's run. With Robert Downey Jr .'s Doctor Doom threatening the multiverse, I imagine there will be plenty of opportunities for Gambit to put those playing cards to work.

" No Me Without You " director Janno Jürgens became fascinated by the love-hate relationship between sisters.

"There's something deeply primal about it," he said.

"A sister or brother can be the person closest to you, but also your very first rival. You share your parents, your home, your childhood and your memories with them, but you also have to share love and attention." In the film, written by Jürgens and Anti Naulainen, a tragedy brings two estranged sisters (Eva Koldits and Katariina Unt) together. Ridden with guilt and moral ambiguity, they embark on a haunting emotional journey.

Jürgens wasn't immediately drawn to the story, he admitted. But eventually, he found his way in.

"After my first feature, ‘Rain,' I realized I really enjoyed watching darker psychological thrillers. I had always been drawn to the genre. Anti's idea could naturally fit into this genre framework."

"We carry grievances, guilt and memories with us, and we may eventually lose that closeness with the people who matter most to us. This leads me to a very important question: is it possible to restore that unconditional closeness we once had? Can we find our way back to another person, even when an entire abyss has formed between us over the years?" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

He wanted the actresses to participate in the creative process.

"We had many meetings before filming, discussing the screenplay and the characters in great detail. I was particularly interested in the women's perspective. As a result, we made quite a few changes," he explained.

"I had the feeling that, in making this film, we were all venturing into uncharted territory. It was an incredibly fascinating journey, but also a difficult one. When you're moving through unfamiliar terrain, the usual safety nets no longer apply."

He wasn't interested in a straightforward drama.

"I've never been drawn to what happens to be popular, mainstream, safe or easily understood. For me, the interesting things have always been somewhere else," he said, revealing that the odd, supernatural elements in the story brought him a sense of comfort.

"Introducing a broader, almost incomprehensible dimension places these events in an entirely different perspective. It reminds me how small we really are within this vast system that we understand so little about. And how far we still are from fully understanding it."

"Considering the immense scale of the universe, how can we ever claim anything with absolute certainty? How can we be so sure that something that happens to us is merely a coincidence? I'm not saying that a greater plan exists. What interests me is the possibility that our understanding of reality may be extremely limited."

Jürgens would like to see more films that dare to be "bold, unexpected and genuinely interesting."

"Everything has become so instantly and easily accessible. People often justify this by saying that life is already difficult enough, and that what people need is simple entertainment. I don't particularly like that idea," he observed.

"I don't believe that a difficult life should mean simple art. Films increasingly seem to blend into one another, and it's becoming harder and harder to experience something that genuinely surprises or touches you. I miss a certain sense of displacement, unpredictability and uniqueness. Something that takes me, even for a moment, outside the world I already know."

His characters certainly go to dark places. But he wanted to explore whether there's a way out of that. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"The extremity of these situations and the question of how far two sisters would go to achieve their goals fascinated me. If I couldn't see some kind of hope in all this darkness, I'm not sure portraying it would hold much meaning for me."

People can hurt each other terribly, and yet love can still exist between them.

"Family is a very particular kind of place in that sense. What has interested me most is the question of whether love can survive even when almost everything else has been destroyed."

articles.content:
Channel 4 boss Priya Dogra has been quizzed by British MPs over the proliferation of sexual abuse scandals currently plaguing the local television industry.

Dogra, who joined Channel 4 last December, was cross-examined at a Department for Culture, Media and Sport meeting Tuesday morning alongside the network's chair Geoff Cooper.

Committee chair Caroline Dinenage opened the meeting with questioning about Brand, saying she had spoken to one of his victims, pseudonymously called "Bella," a former Channel 4 employee. After Brand was found guilty of sexually assaulting her during a video shoot for the network in 2009, Bella said in her victim impact statement she felt Channel 4 had "brushed it under the carpet." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Taylor Swift Ties Grammy Record for Consecutive Album of the Year Nominations Olivia Rodrigo, Katseye and Sienna Spiro to Be Honored at Variety’s 10th Annual Hitmakers Event

According to Dinenage, Bella complained again in 2023 after Channel 4 broadcast a documentary about Brand as part of the Sunday Times investigation that eventually led to him being charged with multiple counts of abuse. He was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual misconduct earlier this month.

"Her complaint was not investigated properly in 2009," Dogra acknowledged. "It should have been. It wasn't escalated properly. Alex [Mahon, Dogra's predecessor at Channel 4] apologized for that. That apology stands, and it shouldn't have happened." She added the network has since strengthened its whistle-blowing protocols.

But Dinenage interrupted to point out that despite her complaint being ignored in 2009, Bella had complained again in 2023 to Channel 4, when the network had pledged to hold an internal investigation into Brand. According to Dinenage, Bella described that inquiry as "shambolic and a whitewash." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"When Bella made her complaints in 2023, again it was not handled properly, and it's almost unforgivable that happened twice," Dogra said, adding shortly after: "I'm not sure we can apologize enough as an organization for putting her through that twice. We have apologized in public in the past and in private."

She noted later during the Q&A session that when Bella originally complained, "There were no findings at that stage of Russell Brand ‘s behavior. There was sort of rumor and speculation, but there was no real finding. That has now changed."

In addition to additional protocols, the CEO said she has also made it mandatory for all production companies Channel 4 works with to sign up to the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority.

Dogra was also quizzed over its hiring practices, given Brand's behavior was overlooked or even enabled by many people in the industry. "In media, we create stars. That's what TV does, that's what film does, and they can appear larger than life," she said. "The backbone of this industry is freelancers, and they generally work on short-term contracts, and that sort of exacerbates, if you will, the power imbalance." She said the network is "creating more resources" for freelancers to help "spot patterns early on."

Dogra also said that "as an industry," networks and companies would need to show "that commercial interests do not override our principles" and that broadcasters would need to be prepared to walk away "from a big show" or a "big personality" because it does not align with its values. "I've had to do that on a recent show," she added, referring to her recent decision to cancel "Married at First Sight U.K." after allegations of sexual abuse were made by some of the contestants.

Asked why she decided to cancel the show following the results of two reviews, commissioned by Channel 4, to determine whether its welfare protocols were adequate, Dogra said "I felt that the wholesale implementation of those recommendations [in the reports] would lead to a completely different show."

She also said she was "uncomfortable" with "some aspects of the recommendations," such as 24/7 recording for monitoring safety and double locking rooms and bathrooms. "I didn't feel that was a show that I wanted to be making," Dogra said, adding the show's "hefty program budget" would be reinvested in new content. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But she admitted that as one of Channel 4's most popular shows, "Married at First Sight" was "incredibly commercially attractive for us. I'm not going to sugarcoat that."

"It was a very profitable show, and therefore, if it's profitable, it pays for all sorts of other programming…. And so to say that it won't be a loss to the financials would be wrong. Of course, it will."

During the almost two-hour long session, Dogra also noted that, following allegations about comedian David Walliams, who is now being investigated for historic sexual offences, the network had "removed any programs" in which he featured.

Fubo had 6 million North American subscribers in the prior-year fourth quarter. The overall subscriber base now represents customers for Fubo ‘s live TV streaming services, including Fubo and Hulu + Live TV, after closing a merger deal with Disney.

articles.title: 5 Shows That Are Better Than They Should Be Thanks to Their Cast, Including a Series Saved by Netflix
articles.summary: Sometimes you start watching a show and realize the story isn't appealing or, while the writing has its merits, it isn't exactly brilliant overall. This happens more often than you might think, but somehow, you find yourself getting more invested and notice it's mostly because of the characters. Yes, in some cases, the cast is […]
articles.content:
Here is a list of series that were loved by audiences (at least by a large portion of them), and had some questionable quality, failed to live up to their own premises , or featured flaws that were just too hard to overlook, but their casts made everything work.

For a long time, How to Get Away with Murder was a series that kept people hooked, as each season relied on flash-forwards to build suspense. On the other hand, the writing wasn't always as strong as it could have been . It often felt like the show was competing with itself to come up with the next big twist, which worked, but only for so long. The story follows Annalise Keating (Viola Davis), a criminal defense attorney and law professor who selects five students to work with her on real cases. What none of them expects, though, is that this experience will eventually pull all of them into a series of crimes and situations they'll do just about anything to keep hidden.

The plot is then driven by investigations, drama, and conflicts that often put everyone in difficult situations. However, not everything is so convincing, and some moments can feel like too much just for the sake of making an impact. Still, one thing that's hard to deny is that a big reason audiences stuck with it for so long was its cast — especially Davis, who pretty much carried every episode with a performance that was even better than the material called for. Thanks to her bringing so much depth to her character, you might not even remember that How to Get Away with Murder had its weaker moments. But the rest of the cast also deserves credit for making the dynamic between the students intriguing all the time.

In the beginning, The Walking Dead was a worldwide phenomenon, to the point that plenty of people would religiously tune in every Sunday for a new episode . But at some point, the show started losing its way, with behind-the-scenes changes and different directions for the plot that gradually drove more and more fans away over its 11-season run. The story begins with Rick Grimes (Andrew Lincoln), a police officer who wakes up from a coma to discover that the world has been overrun by zombies . And after finding other survivors, he takes on the responsibility of leading the group in search of safety, only to realize that humans can be pretty dangerous and violent as well. And before some of the actors started leaving the show, their performances had already gotten you attached to their characters.

Alongside Lincoln, Norman Reedus and Melissa McBride, as Daryl and Carol, were some of the big standouts from the very start, to the point where you could find yourself caring more about what happened to them than about the overall storyline. The cast was so good that even characters who initially didn't seem to have much to offer got room to develop, and you wanted to see more of them . Plus, you probably had your own favorites, and no matter how many others died, you kept rooting for the ones you cared about. That's what helped keep The Walking Dead going for so long, even as it started to decline because of repetitive drama, stories that dragged on longer than they should have, and the simple fact that zombies took a backseat to human rivalries .

If you watch a few episodes of Suits , you'll realize the show doesn't have a complicated formula. You meet Mike (Patrick J. Adams) , a young man with a photographic memory and a natural talent for law who lands a job at a New York law firm despite never having attended law school. Harvey (Gabriel Macht), the lawyer who decides to hire him, knows about the lie but is willing to take the risk, setting up a partnership that has to remain a secret. And whenever someone threatens to expose the truth, the two spend most of the episode trying to find a way out, only for everything to get resolved before another complication comes along to keep the story moving.

Looking at the series as a whole, it's entertaining, but it relies almost entirely on that formula, which makes the situations too predictable. In theory, it's an idea that only works temporarily, because if Mike's secret ever gets exposed, the dynamic of the show has to change. But even when you notice that, you keep watching, and that's because of the ridiculously charismatic cast — and it's not just the leads. The supporting characters have strong personalities and are always stealing the spotlight, even when professional tensions turn into personal matters. Basically, the whole cast has amazing chemistry. In fact, Suits even gained a bigger following after it ended, which shows just how much people kept enjoying it .

You know what it means to be creative? Once Upon a Time had exactly that going for it with its premise: bringing together famous classic fairy-tale characters in an apparently ordinary town, where they have to deal with problems that are very different from what we'd naturally expect from them. The story begins when Emma Swan (Jennifer Morrison) arrives in Storybrooke and discovers that the town's residents are actually characters whose memories were erased by a curse. Then, the show starts exploring several versions of these stories, introducing new figures that you have known for ages. However, eventually, you really need to be patient with just how much lore the series keeps piling up.

The approach leads to some great moments that keep you invested, especially because the story itself taps into the audience's nostalgia. But the writing can't maintain the same level of quality all the way through, and the special effects don't always help either. Still, if you've watched Once Upon a Time , you probably remember it quite fondly, almost like a comfort show. And do you know why? The cast: it's enormous, but easily the production's biggest achievement, no wonder the Evil Queen (Lana Parrilla) became a fan favorite (Rumplestiltskin (Robert Carlyle) and Captain Hook (Colin O'Donoghue) are other standouts). With so many found-family dynamics between the characters, you get attached to their relationships and care about what happens to them until you find yourself bingeing every episode .

Ask someone what they think of Lucifer , and there's a good chance you'll hear some negative opinions. It's not exactly a show that's well-regarded, even if it's far from terrible. The story revolves around Lucifer Morningstar (Tom Ellis) , the Devil himself, who starts working as a police consultant after meeting Chloe (Lauren German), a detective who seems to be immune to his powers of persuasion. Meanwhile, he also has to deal with problems involving his siblings, his father, and the consequences of letting go of his responsibilities in Hell. The series follows that hybrid structure, with a different case in each episode while a storyline develops alongside it — but that's the main problem.

Shows like The X-Files and House became iconic using that same structure, but they knew how to develop their identities, character arcs, and stories. Lucifer , on the other hand, often relied on the formula and struggled to go beyond the conventional police format, even though its premise had so much potential. Still, you keep watching because of Ellis: much like Davis in How to Get Away with Murder , he has the ability to embody his character on every level, and without his performance, many of the jokes and situations that make the show good wouldn't have the same effect. And even when some of the supporting storylines fall a little flat, the cast does its best to make them more engaging. It's no wonder the show got canceled only to be brought back by Netflix after fans campaigned to save it.

articles.title: Disney Expects to Increase Annual Content Spend to $26 Billion Next Year
articles.summary: The increase in spending is due to more international fare, sports rights, and the timing of feature film production.
articles.content:
The Walt Disney Co. isn't slowing down when it comes to spending major cash on original content.

The company disclosed Tuesday in its quarterly earnings report that it expects to spend $26 billion on content in fiscal 2027 (which started this quarter), up 9 percent from the $24 billion or so it spent in fiscal 2026.

Disney says that the increase in spending is being driven by increased investment in international programming, growing sports rights costs, and the timing of feature film production spend. Disney has been pursuing more international programming as it seeks to grow its streaming business abroad, while sports rights like the NBA and NFL continue to rise like clockwork every year. articles.title: These (Alleged) Reality TV Lies From AGT To Bar Rescue Will Have You Appalled
articles.summary: These are some wild stories I didn't expect.
articles.content:
Even the best reality TV shows can be accused of being scripted, and while not every claim is substantiated, there are a lot of allegations. Personally, like many others, I might be taken aback on the off chance that such a claim turns out to be true. Just recently, I found two stories from people who allegedly got a first-hand look at the inner workings of America's Got Talent and Bar Rescue , and they're fascinating to read.

It's not uncommon for reality TV show subjects to complain about receiving unflattering or dishonest edits. Over the years, stars have alleged that producers can get the response they want out of them and then edit the footage to make it appear they said something entirely different from what they meant. If AGT actually engaged in this, it wouldn't be different from claims against many other shows on the 2026 TV schedule . Regardless, this should be a gentle reminder for viewers not to believe everything they see.

From there, the writer claimed the bar's owners removed all the furniture and revamped the menu with new cocktails. His wife apparently stood in line to attend the reopening and was instructed before entering that she could only order the signature cocktail.

The whole account really makes me rethink the times I've seen Jon Taffer give advice on how to fix a bar . Of course, this is all alleged, and it's not like there are receipts or concrete proof of these claims. It isn't necessarily hard to believe, but given the lack of hard evidence or even any identifiable information, I'd take it with a grain of salt.

articles.content:
Whether such Hollywood films as Christopher Nolan's Tenet , Venice 2026 winner Woman Unknown or such series as Paramount+ spy thriller The Agency , the BBC's War & Peace , and Apple TV's Star City – the Baltic countries of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia have been among the locations that international productions have turned to, bringing global audiences a look and taste of the region.

Film and TV craft experts have brought their skills to international and local crews alike.

With the 25th edition of the Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event (ITBE) market, part of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF), currently shining a spotlight on the Baltic region, THR decided to check in with some creatives who have brought their talents to film and series you may well recognize. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Dual Oscar Winner Christopher Hampton Calls Glenn Close Honorary Oscar "the Least They Can Do," Says AI Is Just "a Super Google" Music IVE, BINI, KiiiKiii, SB19, LiSA and Babymetal Score Grammy Nominations in New Asian Pop Category

Meet some of the faces you want to or should know below.

Ingrīda Nagle, location manager, Latvia You may have seen her work in: Woman Unknown (the first Latvian co-production in the main competition at Venice where it won the Golden Lion. The Latvian capital Riga is standing in for post-war Denmark); Gomorrah ; Oleg ; Dogs Don't Wear Pants .

How long have you been working in your field, and what first inspired you to do this kind of creative work? I have been working in the film industry since 2009. It was a very interesting and challenging turn of events in my life, and I got into the industry through a fortunate coincidence. I was invited to work as a Production Assistant (PA) on the international biographical television film The Courageous Heart of Irena Sendler , which was shot in Latvia. In this role, I had to prove my abilities and versatility, which I handled successfully throughout the project. I received great recommendations and, inspired by my colleagues, began focusing specifically on location management. Over the years, working on many different and challenging projects, I realized that I truly enjoy this work. As my skills developed, I found it increasingly rewarding. It is worth noting that before starting my career in film, I graduated from the Riga Film Studio Acting School, so in a way, working in cinema was already waiting for me. I am deeply grateful for this twist of fate, which fundamentally changed my professional career. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

What are some of the big international productions you have worked on? How did they find you and your skills, and how did they hire you? I have worked on a number of notable feature films and series. Among them are films such as Dogs Don't Wear Pants ; Oleg ; The Exalted ; Modris ; the series Gomorrah ; The Invisible Fight , and most recently, the award-winning feature Woman Unknown . For the most part, producers reach out to me based on recommendations regarding my ability to think out of the box, offer unconventional location ideas, as well as my multitasking abilities, communication skills, and professional attitude. In the film industry, accuracy, the ability to navigate complex situations, finding quick solutions, while maintaining creativity and a good sense of humor, are highly valued – and I believe I possess all of these qualities.

Do you focus on either local or international work now or how do you choose projects? Currently, I am working on several large-scale international projects. I am pleased to say that my professional capabilities and level of work have [earned] a high degree of trust. However, whenever time and capacity allow, I also really enjoy working with local, talented directors and on smaller-scale projects. In these projects, where the crew is compact and creative freedom is high, a special “film family” feeling is created, which brings immense satisfaction in being an important part of making the movie.

Throughout my life, I have covered most distances on foot, and that is precisely how I have discovered truly wonderful and unique locations. Be open to challenges, read plenty of books to develop your communication skills. Don't be afraid to make mistakes! Disney says December will see the addition of TikTok creator videos to Disney+ as well as the completion of the long-in-the-works integration of Hulu programming.

The streaming initiatives come as the company preps for a major film release, Avengers: Doomsday , on December 18.

The outlook was part of Disney's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report, with the quarterly numbers easily beating Wall Street estimates .

“We are also adding more vertical video, live sports, and podcasts to the platform, while continuing to explore other emerging content genres,” the earnings release said.

At the same time of the TikTok influx, subscribers to Disney+ will have a “fully unified” experience as the integration of Hulu programming into the mother ship is completed.
